title: Will India’s Growth Keep Defying Global Headwinds?
text:
Will India’s Growth Keep Defying Global Headwinds?

Tom Miller, Udith Sikand

Gavekal Research | 4 Sep 2026

Once again, the specter of stagflation is haunting the global economy. The resumption in fighting between the United States and Iran has pushed Brent to US$95/bbl, raising inflation expectations and threatening consumption and growth. Bond yields in the US and Europe are hitting multi-year highs—and a multi-decade high in Japan—as markets price in monetary tightening, jacking up borrowing costs on already eye-watering debt loads. But within the gloom there is a shaft of light: faster-than-expected growth in India. “Doomsayers were doomed and India bloomed… yet again!” Prime Minister Narendra Modi crowed.Modi this week described headline GDP growth of 7.8% YoY in the quarter ended June as a “Herculean feat,” delivered in the face of oil-price shocks and supply-chain disruptions. For critics, however, India’s statistical stables retain a whiff of ordure. One senior opposition leader dismissed the GDP numbers as “statistical gymnastics,” accusing the government of using methodological revisions to fix the data while “hiding India’s bleak economic reality.” But criticisms of data manipulation are exaggerated, if not entirely misplaced. India’s economy is in good shape, even if sustained higher oil prices risk dampening Modi’s mood.
